To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the proteasome is involved in the regulation of synaptic strength; (2) the proteasomal degradation of synaptic proteins is required for long-term potentiation (LTP), the most widely studied form of synaptic plasticity; and (3) the proteasomes in dendrites are required for the maintenance of synaptic strength.
proteasomal activity is required for synaptic plasticity and that proteasomal regulation of synapses occurs at the level of individual synapses and in a spatially restricted manner.
proteasome inhibition causes an increase in synaptic strength in a variety of preparations and that this increase in synaptic strength is due to an increase in synaptic protein levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how proteasomal function is controlled at synapses to regulate synaptic plasticity.
the mechanisms that regulate synaptic protein turnover and how these mechanisms are used in the nervous system.
the role of proteasomal activity in synaptic plasticity and how proteasomal function can be regulated in the context of synaptic plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

proteasomes are involved in synaptic plasticity in a number of different ways, and that proteasomes may be involved in a number of processes that are important for the regulation of the protein content of a synapse.
the proteasome is involved in a number of different aspects of synaptic plasticity.
the ubiquitin-protein degradation pathway is an important component of synaptic plasticity and that the proteasome is a major regulator of synaptic protein turnover.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ubiquitin proteosome system (UPS) is an important regulator of the protein content of synaptic terminals and that UPS activity can be regulated by neuronal activity.
the ubiquitin-protesome system is an important player in synaptic plasticity and memory.
proteasomal degradation of synaptic proteins is an important mechanism to regulate synaptic plasticity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein degradation by the proteasome is an important component of synaptic plasticity.
the ubiquitin proteolysis system can regulate synaptic strength over different time scales.
protein degradation via the proteasome can be a regulated process and can be used to control synaptic strength.
